summary.intent: Run the full post-execute-phase ship loop for Phase 66 (API schema cutover, publish gate, tombstone) autonomously: verify → secure → validate → simplify → SDK E2E → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews.
summary.outcome: PR #584 opened, all audit gates passed (SECURED 17/17, Nyquist-compliant, SDK E2E green), greptile review threads resolved, and two CI failures (coverage-threshold regressions + SDK E2E timing flake) diagnosed and fixed; coverage workflow restored 75 deleted specs across 5 files before transcript end.

repo: The Phase 66 cutover deleted all 5 shares spec files without rewriting them, leaving shares.controller.ts / share-invites.controller.ts / invites.controller.ts / shares.service.ts at 0% coverage and dropping global branches below the 78% jest threshold — a pattern to watch on any module-reshaping cutover.

jest's global coverageThreshold excludes per-file-path entries from the global computation, so individual controller-threshold failures don't necessarily drag the global number — but leaving large modules at 0% does.

`api:generate` reformats openapi.json from single-line to multi-line arrays with no semantic change; always diff-and-revert to avoid noise commits (the pre-commit hook only blocks on real surface changes).

Migration files can get prettier-reformatted as a side effect of the api:generate lint pass; reverting that reformatting locally is correct, but automated commits can slip it through, causing CI Lint failures on the next run.

The mock-ipns-routing at-floor serve is fire-and-forget (publish to delegated routing is async); SDK E2E Test 15 needs a bounded poll for eventual consistency rather than an immediate assert — this caused a CI-only flake.
The `verify:post` hooks for `secure-phase` and `validate-phase` were not enabled in the local GSD config, so the audit gates had to be run directly without the enforcement wrapper.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body must be patched via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
After `gh pr create`, the release bot pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the branch; always `git fetch` + rebase before the next push or it will be rejected.

All 9 Phase 66 PLANs contained parseable `<threat_model>` blocks (`register_authored_at_plan_time: true`), enabling the short-circuit rule at ASVS L1 — but a real open threat (T-66-E1) required a full auditor pass regardless.

code.finding: T-66-E1: claim path checked dto.writeDescriptorRef without gating on invite.writeDescriptorRef; a read-only invite could be exploited to obtain a write grant by supplying writeDescriptorRef in the claim payload. Fixed by nulling out the claimer value when invite.writeDescriptorRef is null.

tombstoneRecord discarded the TypeORM update's `affected` count and always returned 200, making non-existent/unowned/already-tombstoned record requests indistinguishable from success. Fixed to throw NotFoundException when affected === 0.

syncIpnsRecordSequence lacked a tombstonedAt: IsNull() guard, creating a race window where a tombstoned record could have its sequence bumped by the republish job. Fixed by adding the guard; the corresponding spec assertion also needed updating to reflect the new criteria.

The new tombstone endpoint was the only handler in the controller without a @Throttle decorator; all sibling endpoints (publish, publish-batch, unenroll, resolve) had one. Added @Throttle to close the inconsistency on a phase-new destructive endpoint.

rootIpnsName used the loose /^k[a-z0-9]+$/ regex instead of the canonical strict IPNS name validator used by sibling DTOs (resolve, tombstone). Tightened to the canonical pattern; same fix applied to create-invite.dto.ts:17.

Test 15 at-floor serve asserted immediately after network-record publish, which is fire-and-forget; the resolve can return null if delegated routing hasn't propagated yet. Fixed with a bounded poll (6s, 500ms interval) for eventual consistency.

_publicKey? param was unused (underscore-flagged) in a private upsertIpnsRecord method with a single caller; safe to remove. The publicKeyBytes variable used for sig verification is a separate binding at a different layer.

workflow: Always adversarially verify subagent results: run the authored spec yourself, confirm only spec files were created (no impl touched), and check the T-66-E1 assertion would actually fail against the pre-fix code before trusting the GAPS FILLED report.

When a coverage failure is reported in CI, read the full log tail — early lines show only passing tests; the threshold violation lines appear at the very end and are easy to miss when grepping for FAIL.

A workflow fan-out (5 parallel spec-authoring agents) with a subsequent authoritative full jest --coverage run is the right pattern for restoring deleted coverage across multiple files — but the authoritative run is mandatory; scoped per-file runs can mask cross-file interactions.
Prettier auto-formatting issues in new spec files will be caught by CI Lint but not by ts-jest (which only type-checks); always run eslint --fix on generated specs before committing.
The commit helper can report success while the pre-commit hook's final step times out; verify with git log --oneline -1 before retrying, or you risk an amend on the wrong commit.
GitHub thread reply mutations are occasionally flaky (timeouts); always re-query reviewThreads after mutations to confirm resolved=true and reply presence before marking step done.

For e2e CI flakes caused by fire-and-forget async operations, reproduce locally 3x before concluding it's a flake vs. regression — a 3/3 local pass with a mechanistic explanation (async propagation) is sufficient evidence.

friction: CodeRabbit CLI hit a service connection error on the first invocation; required a retry with no code change.

api:generate reformatted openapi.json with no semantic change, then failed on a pre-existing eslint error in a gitignored Astro generated file — required a careful diff + revert to avoid committing noise.
Pre-existing prettier drift in a migration file slipped through local pre-commit hooks via an automated commit, causing CI Lint to fail only after pushing — required a separate format-fix commit.

The GSD secure-phase and validate-phase enforcement hooks were not enabled in config, so the full workflow process had to be manually interpreted and driven rather than using the hook-gated automation.
GitHub thread reply mutations timed out on P1, requiring a separate re-post step after confirming P2's reply landed.
The CI Test failure was a coverage-threshold failure (not a test failure), making it look like passing tests at first glance; the actual threshold violation lines only appeared at the log tail.
The republish.service.spec.ts assertion on the update criteria needed to be updated to match the new tombstone guard — a legitimate but subtle test-maintenance burden from the security fix.
